source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 16 January 1931, p. 9 ("Belfast municipal elections: Shankill and Dock results"); Belfast News-Letter, 6 January 1931, p. 9 ("Ulster municipal elections (continued from page 7)")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: unopposed members are the only nominee in their ward in the News-Letter's list of nominations (page images checked for Clifton and Falls); votes from the News-Letter's results (INA OCR), checked against the Irish News for Dock; where the OCR of a vote is garbled the figure used is the one that agrees with both the printed valid votes and the printed majority

note: Annual election of one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the member retiring in rotation), nominations Monday 5 January, poll Thursday 15 January 1931. Thirteen members were returned unopposed; Dock and Shankill were contested, and the Unionists took Dock from the Socialists (Belfast News-Letter, 6 and 16 January 1931). Both were new candidates. The OCR of the votes and valid votes is garbled; 4,366 and 2,605 are the figures that agree with the printed majority (1,761) and valid votes (6,971).
